Join us and be part of this journey towards greater opportunities and brighter futures.

Concentrix is seeking a Sr. Software Architect (NiCE CXone & Cognigy) to lead the design, implementation, integration, and evolution of enterprise customer experience solutions.

This is a senior customer-facing technical leadership role responsible for architecting and delivering scalable NiCE CXone and Cognigy solutions across complex enterprise environments. The successful candidate will combine deep technical expertise with strong consulting, delivery, and problem-solving skills to help clients modernize their customer engagement platforms.

You will work directly with clients, business stakeholders, architects, engineers, and delivery teams to translate business requirements into secure, scalable, AI-enabled customer experience solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Solution Architecture & Technical Leadership

  • Design scalable, secure, and high-performing solutions utilizing NiCE CXone, Cognigy, and related enterprise technologies.
  • Lead architecture reviews and provide direction on critical technical decisions.
  • Establish architecture standards, implementation patterns, and technical best practices.
  • Identify technical risks, dependencies, and opportunities across applications, integrations, infrastructure, and data platforms.

Implementation & Delivery

  • Lead end-to-end implementation of NiCE CXone and Cognigy solutions from discovery through production deployment.
  • Design and oversee integrations with CRM, telephony, workforce engagement, AI, data, and enterprise platforms.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve complex platform, integration, and performance issues.
  • Ensure solutions meet requirements for scalability, security, availability, maintainability, and supportability.

Hands-On Development

  • Configure and implement NiCE CXone platform capabilities.
  • Design, develop, and deploy Cognigy conversational AI applications, workflows, and integrations.
  • Build reusable accelerators, integration patterns, and technical assets that improve delivery efficiency and consistency.
  • Support testing, deployment, monitoring, and operational readiness activities.

Consulting & Collaboration

  • Partner with clients and internal stakeholders to define solution strategies, technical roadmaps, and implementation plans.
  • Partner with sales, solutioning, and delivery teams on client pursuits, technical workshops, architecture assessments, and implementation planning.
  • Mentor architects, engineers, and technical consultants.
  • Contribute to technical estimates, solution design, and architecture discussions for strategic initiatives.

Qualifications

Required

  • 10+ years of experience in customer experience technologies, CCaaS solution architecture, software engineering, systems integration, or enterprise technology delivery.
  • Hands-on implementation experience with NiCE CXone.
  • Experience designing, implementing, or integrating conversational AI solutions, AI agents, virtual assistants, generative AI technologies, or enterprise automation platforms, including Cognigy or similar technologies.
  • Strong understanding of APIs, integrations, CRM, workforce management, cloud platforms, security, and modern application architectures.
  • Experience leading complex technical implementations and multi-disciplinary delivery teams.
  • Strong communication, consulting, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, Management Information Systems, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Strongly Preferred

  • NICE CXone Certified Implementation Professional (CIP) certification or equivalent NICE implementation credentials.
  • NICE CXone implementation certifications in ACD/IVR, AI Routing, Digital Experience, Agent Embedded/Integrated, or related CXone modules.
  • NICE Certified Implementation Engineer (NCIE) certifications in Interaction Analytics, Workforce Management, Quality Management, Performance Management, or related NICE solutions
  • Cognigy Associate, Engineer, Conversation Design, or related Cognigy certifications.
  • Experience with Amazon Connect, Genesys Cloud CX, Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, ServiceNow, or related customer engagement platforms.
  • AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud certifications.
  • Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Software Engineering, Business Technology, or a related discipline.

Why Join Concentrix?

This role offers a unique opportunity to shape and deliver next-generation customer experience solutions at global scale. You will work across NiCE CXone, Cognigy, AI, automation, cloud, and customer engagement technologies while helping some of the world's leading brands modernize their customer experience ecosystems.

You'll have the opportunity to influence architecture standards, accelerate AI adoption, and help define how global organizations leverage CCaaS, conversational AI, and intelligent automation to transform customer experiences.

If you enjoy solving complex technical challenges, working directly with clients, and balancing architecture leadership with hands-on delivery, you'll thrive in this role.

The base salary for this position is $122,001- $191,715 plus incentives that align with individual and company performance. Actual salaries will vary based on work location, qualifications, skills, education, experience, and competencies. Benefits available to eligible employees in this role include medical, dental, and vision insurance, comprehensive employee assistance program, 401(k) retirement plan, paid time off and holidays and paid learning days.

Employment Type: Full-Time / Part-Time (Non-Exempt)

Pay Range: $16/hr and up depending on experience


The Opportunity


We’re hiring leaders for our service centers — people who want to run a business, not just work a shift. This is a hands-on leadership role: you’ll be on the floor with your team, driving sales and service performance, developing people, and owning the guest experience.


Every store leader starts in our Manager-in-Training (MIT) program. No prior automotive experience is required — we’ll teach you our operations, systems, and leadership standards from the ground up. Depending on your experience, you may step into an Assistant Manager role or move onto the Store Manager track. Many of our managers started as technicians. We promote from within.


Your Path: Manager-in-Training Program


• All new store leaders start in MIT — no prior Jiffy Lube or automotive experience required

• Learn daily store operations, sales and service processes, and our systems through hands-on, in-store training

• Work alongside experienced managers and leaders to build the skills to run your own location

• Progression is based on successful completion of the program and demonstrated readiness


What You’ll Do


• Lead daily store operations including sales, service, and financial performance

• Lead by example — deliver exceptional customer service and drive results on the floor

• Drive revenue growth by coaching your team on service recommendations and sales execution

• Coach, train, and develop team members to improve performance and engagement

• Manage key performance metrics including sales, labor, and profitability

• Recruit, interview, hire, and onboard new team members

• Build a strong, accountable, and positive team culture

• Manage scheduling, staffing, and labor to hit budget and service targets

• Oversee inventory management, cash controls, and operational processes

• Resolve customer concerns and escalated guest issues

• Maintain a clean, safe, and fully operational facility

• Ensure compliance with company policies, procedures, and safety standards

• Run the store independently in the Store Manager’s absence


What We’re Looking For


• 1+ year of leadership or supervisory experience preferred — automotive, retail, restaurant, or service industry all translate

• Willingness to complete our Manager-in-Training program

• Strong leadership and team development skills

• Comfortable managing performance metrics and driving business results

• Strong customer service and sales mindset

• Ability to multitask and prioritize in a fast-paced environment

• Strong communication and problem-solving skills

• Basic computer and operational system skills

• Valid driver’s license and clean driving record

• Ability to work flexible schedules, including weekends as needed


Work Environment & Physical Requirements


• Ability to stand for extended periods of time

• Work in a service shop environment with exposure to noise, fumes, and varying temperatures

• Ability to lift up to 50 pounds

• Frequent movement including bending, lifting, and working with tools and equipment

• Ability to drive customer vehicles


Why Join Our Team?


• Competitive weekly pay

• Bonus and incentive opportunities

• Medical, dental, and vision insurance

• 401(k) with company match

• Paid time off starting Day 1

• Employee discounts

• Industry-leading training programs

• Clear career advancement opportunities

• Team-oriented, supportive work environment


Equal Opportunity Employer

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law.

title: Compensation Analyst
description:
The Compensation Analyst designs and runs Omilia's sales compensation programme end to end, from plan architecture through to the reporting infrastructure that keeps it accurate every cycle. This role owns both strategy and execution - building compensation plans and SPIFFs from scratch, then running the mechanisms that calculate, track and report on them. Reporting into Revenue Operations, this role partners closely with Sales, Finance and Payroll to keep compensation accurate, timely and aligned to revenue goals.

Accountabilities

  • Own end-to-end design of sales compensation plans and incentive structures aligned to revenue goals.
  • Own the full SPIFF programme lifecycle, from design and launch through payout and ROI retrospective.
  • Own the comp calculation, payout and reporting infrastructure that keeps compensation accurate every cycle.
  • Own compensation plan documentation, quota assignments and plan change history.
  • Own cross-functional alignment with Sales, Finance and Payroll on plan design, quota setting and payout accuracy.

Key Responsibilities

Design and build sales compensation plans and incentive structures aligned to revenue goals.

  • Model plan scenarios and payout economics to test affordability and behavioural impact before rollout.
  • Recommend plan changes based on performance data and market benchmarking.
  • Design, build and launch SPIFF programmes, defining mechanics, eligibility, targets and payout structure.
  • Track SPIFF performance in-flight and report on ROI against target behaviour.
  • Run the end-to-end comp calculation and payout process each cycle.
  • Build and maintain the reporting infrastructure and mechanisms needed to run comp accurately at scale.
  • Build dashboards and reports for comp attainment, plan performance and SPIFF ROI.
  • Partner with Finance on accruals, forecasting and comp cost analysis.
  • Partner with RevOps on the CRM data integrity that feeds every calculation, and flag design issues, payout errors or gaming risk before they escalate.

Requirements

Required:

  • Experience designing and administering sales compensation plans in a B2B SaaS environment.
  • Direct experience building and running SPIFF programmes end to end.
  • Strong Excel and analytical modelling skills.
  • Comfortable owning both the strategic design and the operational mechanics of a compensation programme.
  • High attention to detail, given the direct link to employee pay accuracy.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with comp/ICM platforms (e.g. Xactly, CaptivateIQ, Spiff).
  • Experience running compensation across multiple currencies or regions.
  • Background partnering directly with Finance on comp accruals and forecasting.

Omilia Note

- Contribute actively and effectively as an integrated team member.
- Act as an Omilia ambassador in all interactions.

title: Zero Trust Network Engineer
description:
Description

Quantum Sky is searching for a forward-thinking and self-motivated Zero Trust Network Engineer to focus on the deployment and configuration of a government client’s Zero Trust Broker tools in their environment. This exciting role requires an appetite for learning, superior attention to detail, the ability to meet tight deadlines, great organizational skills, and the ability to work in a highly collaborative work environment. You will possess the ability to complete complex tasks and projects quickly with little to no guidance, react with appropriate urgency to situations that require a quick turnaround, and take effective action without having to know the total picture.

Responsibilities:

  • Analyze the client’s current network architecture
  • Develop future-state network architecture and technical documentation
  • Perform deployment and configuration of zero trust broker tools for access to the internet and private applications
  • Support the integration of the zero-trust broker tools with other security tools, including identity management, SIEM, and EDR tools
  • Perform ongoing operations and maintenance of the zero-trust broker tools, including providing patching and end-user support
  • Perform onboarding/offboarding of device logs according to operational requirements
  • Collaborate with SIEM engineers to ensure logs are onboarding and maintained in the SIEM tool
  • Provide support for ongoing SIEM tuning and use case development
  • Perform research and lead proof of concept efforts to determine where additional technologies may be necessary
  • Provide advisory support to client leadership on responses to new network requirements and regulatory mandates (such as executive orders, emergency directives, binding operational directives, and data calls from governance and oversight bodies

Qualifications

Required:

  • Minimum six (6) years of network or cybersecurity expertise
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience
  • Direct experience with deploying, configuring, or maintaining zero trust broker tools, such as Zscaler
  • Experience with providing technical support for network architecture, design, engineering, and maintenance
  • Familiarity with Trusted Internet Connection (TIC) 3.0 guidelines
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills that include the ability to describe highly technical concepts in non-technical terms

Desired:

  • Relevant network security or cybersecurity-related certifications, such as Forrester Zero Trust Strategy
  • CISSP

Clearance: Active Secret Clearance Required

Location: Remote

About Quantum Sky

Compensation:

  • Compensation is unique to each candidate and relative to the skills and experience they bring to the position. The salary range for this position is typically between $155,000-$160,000. This does not guarantee a specific salary as compensation is based upon multiple factors such as education, experience, certifications, and other requirements, and may fall outside of the above-stated range.

Benefits:

  • Highlights of our benefits include Health/Dental/Vision, 401(k) match, Paid Time Off, STD/LTD/Life Insurance, Referral Bonuses, professional development reimbursement, and parental leave.

The world the mission operates in is going post-quantum, contested, and machine-speed. Quantum Sky engineers the advantage across cyber, networks, software, and quantum because the mission demands dominance, not parity. We don't follow the map. We draw it.

At Quantum Sky, we believe that success starts with our people. We foster a collaborative, innovative, and mission-driven environment where every team member plays a critical role in shaping the future of technology. Are you ready to join #TeamQuantumSky?

title: Salesperson
description:
Job Description

What is a Salesperson?

Entry level sales position capable of supporting the DIY business and achieve our sales and service objectives. The role has good knowledge of store systems, basic automotive system knowledge and basic part knowledge. The role has the basic ability to source from stores, hubs, pdq, and external suppliers. The role has in-depth knowledge of the store inventory and maintenance processes. Position can be part time or full time. Fleet safety certification preferred.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Provide excellent selling experience for DIY customer visits and phone calls
  • Achieve personal sales goal and help store achieve its sales goals
  • Provide DIY services including battery installation, testing, wiper installs, etc.
  • Maintain store product and operational standards
  • Responsible for inventory processes including truck put away, shoot outs, cycle counts, Back stock, etc.

Secondary Responsibilities

  • Store Cleanliness including floors, bathrooms, facing, dusting, parking lot
  • General stocking including truck stocking and back stock
  • Safely deliver parts to customers as needed

Success Factors

  • Basic driving and navigation ability
  • Ability to use delivery board system
  • Friendly communication
  • Ability to locate and stock parts
  • Safety knowledge and skills
  • Operating inventory systems and store equipment
  • Parts and automotive system knowledge skills
  • Operating POS and Parts lookup systems
  • Expert at testing and diagnostic equipment for DIY service

Essential Job Skills Necessary for Success as a Salesperson

  • Speak and write English (Spanish a plus); communicate effectively and build strong relationships with customers, peers and management
  • Read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, parts catalogs, and procedure manuals
  • Use basic math accurately: add, subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals
  • Ability to work an assortment of days, evenings, and weekends as needed

Prior Experience that Sets a Salesperson up for Success

  • 2-3 years of successful sales experience in a diverse retail environment, providing superior customer experiences

Physical Demands

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee will predominantly be walking or standing. The employee is required to be able to talk and hear, and use hands and fingers to handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

Work Environment

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is usually working inside; however, they will occasionally be outside and exposed to various weather conditions while performing such tasks as installing batteries and wiper blades. The employee is also occasionally exposed to moving mechanical parts; high, precarious places; toxic or caustic chemicals; risk of electrical shock; explosives; and vibration. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

title: Social Services Designee

Known for its cultural diversity, West Rogers Park is home to residents who speak over 80 languages, offering a unique, community-centered environment. At Astoria Place, we are proud to reflect this diversity, with a dedicated team of professionals, including Russian and Cantonese-speaking staff, who provide personalized care and make our residents feel truly at home.

Our Gold Seal of Approval® from The Joint Commission for Post-Acute Care and Nursing Care showcases our commitment to high-quality healthcare. With state-of-the-art medical care, skilled nursing assistance, and tailored therapies, our expert team ensures that every resident receives the attention and treatment they deserve.

In addition to exceptional healthcare, Astoria Place provides a welcoming environment enriched with spacious suites, restaurant-quality meals, and activities designed to enhance both physical and emotional well-being. Our residents also enjoy easy access to the culturally diverse businesses and services of West Rogers Park, including a variety of international cuisines just steps from the facility.

Are you looking for a rewarding career in Skilled Nursing? We are currently searching for a Social Services Designee to join our friendly, caring and supportive team!

  • *Short-term and long-term disability insurance options.
  • *401K with employer match.
  • Employee concierge program.
  • Employee assistance program.
  • And more!

    *Please note that benefit packages vary based on hours worked.

As a Social Services Designee you will assist in preparing our residents for their future. Your work will ensure our residents receive the high standard of care they have grown to expect at Astoria Place Living & Rehab Center by ensuring our residents social and emotional needs are met during their stay, coordinating resident discharges and participating in resident care conferences. Our residents will depend on your knowledge, skills, and attention to detail to ensure they are comfortable and safe.

To be eligible for consideration applicants should have:

As a minimum, a high school diploma or equivalent and two (2) years of experience in a Social Worker role preferably in a healthcare setting. Prior Social Services Designee experience in a Skilled Nursing Facility, bachelor’s degree in Social work or similar field and five (5) years of related experience is preferable but we are willing to invest in the right candidate!

If you are an individual who gets satisfaction from knowing they made a difference, stop in or visit https://astoriaplace.com/ to learn more and get your career started

Astoria Place Living and Rehab is located at 6300 N California Ave, Chicago, IL 60659, in the West Rogers Park neighborhood. title: Social Services Director
description:
Healthcare, Dental, Vision

Paid Time Off

Excellent Pay

Your Job

The Social Services Director will be responsible for planning, developing, organizing, evaluating and directing the overall operation of the Social Services department in accordance with the National Association of Social Workers (NASW) Code of Ethics and in compliance with Federal, State, and Local guidelines and regulations, company policies and procedures, and governing agencies. Responsible for fostering a climate, policies and routines that enable residents to maximize their individuality, independence and dignity. This climate should provide residents with the highest practical level of physical, mental and psychosocial well-being and quality of life. Responsible for identifying psychosocial, mental and emotional needs along with providing, developing, and/or aiding in the access of services to meet those needs.

Qualifications

• One year of supervisory social work experience in a healthcare setting working directly with geriatric individuals.

• Minimum of 2 years of nursing experience in a Skilled Nursing Facility preferred.

Principal Responsibilities

• Plans, organizes, implements, evaluates, and directs a comprehensive Social Services program.

• Assist the Social Service Consultant in the planning, developing, organizing, implementing, evaluating, and directing of the social service programs of the facility; Participates in reviewing and setting policies concerning resident care and quality of life; Participates in developing facility social work policies.

• Prepares Social Services department for annual survey.

• Works with Social Services staff, interdisciplinary team, and administration to promote and protect resident rights and the psychological well-being of all residents/residents. Prevents and addresses resident/resident abuse as mandated by law and professional licensure.

• Completes social history and psychosocial assessment for each resident that identifies social, emotional, and psychological needs; Completed relevant parts of the minimum data set (MDS); Utilizes the minimum data set to guide the care plan.

• Maintains accurate and timely documentation which complies with federal/state regulations, The Company Corporate policy, and specific center practices, including, but not limited to, Advanced Directives, Minimum Data Set, Social Service History and Assessment, Raps, Care Plans, Social Service Progress Notes, Behavior Tracking, monitoring of cognitive and psychosocial changes, PASARR and Discharge Planning documentation, and psych services.

• Supports each resident’s/resident’s right to self-determination; Documents resident/resident refusal of services offered; Informs resident/resident of any therapeutic alternatives to the refused service; Involves others, as appropriate, to help educate the resident/resident about the alternatives.

• Participates in the development of a written, interdisciplinary plan of care for each resident that identifies the psychosocial needs/issues of the resident, the goals to be accomplished for those needs/issues, and the appropriate social worker interventions.

• Ensures or provides therapeutic interventions to assist residents in coping with their transition and adjustment to a long-term care facility, including their social, emotional, and psychological needs.

• Ensures or provides support and education to residents/family members/significant others to assist in their understanding of placement and facility issues in addition to referring them to the appropriate social service agencies when the facility does not provide the needed services.

• Coordinates the resident discharge planning process and make referrals for appropriate home care services prior to the resident’s return to the community.

• As part of interdisciplinary care team, identifies discharge teaching needs; Communicates with center team members the estimated discharge date and updating Point Click Care; Makes referrals as needed for post discharge care to appropriate agencies and suppliers.

• Initiates and participates in completion of Discharge Transition Plan & Discharge packet materials and orienting the resident/resident and family around the process.

• Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or assigned at any time with or without notice.

title: Lot Attendant
description:
Kendall Toyota of Anchorage has an immediate opening for a Lot Attendant to join our team. Come join a hardworking team who strives each day to make sure our customers are happy and that our dealership is looking great with the vehicles staying test-drive ready!


Some of the benefits of working with Kendall as a Lot Attendant are:

Our employees are members of the Kendall family, who share our same goals and passions. Ideal candidates are confident, driven people who are excited to grow and succeed with one of the most successful automotive dealerships in the Pacific Northwest. If you are looking for a rewarding career, we would like to meet you and start something great!

title: Job Title: Specialist Static and Package Equipment Engineer   - Offshore Project
description:
Title:

Job Title: Specialist Static and Package Equipment Engineer - Offshore Project

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR!

The KBR team of teams delivers future-forward science, technology and engineering solutions and mission-critical services that help governments and companies around the world accomplish their most important objectives, while also helping achieve their sustainability goals. KBR Sustainable Technology Solutions provides holistic and value-added solutions across the entire asset life cycle. These include world-class licensed process technologies, differentiated advisory services, deep technical domain expertise, energy transition solutions, high-end design and engineering capabilities, and smart solutions to optimize planned and operating assets.

Job Title: Specialist Static and Package Equipment Engineer - Offshore Project

KBR is growing its Project Management Consultancy (PMC) team for an exciting, high‑profile offshore development in Abu Dhabi.

Job Purpose

Provide specialist engineering expertise for the design, specification, review, procurement, fabrication, testing, installation, and commissioning of static and packaged equipment for offshore oil and gas facilities. Ensure compliance with ADNOC standards, international codes, project specifications, HSE requirements, and project schedule objectives throughout all project phases.

Key Responsibilities

Engineering & Design

Lead and review the engineering design of static equipment including:

    • Pressure Vessels
    • Columns and Towers
    • Heat Exchangers
    • Storage Tanks
    • Pig Launchers and Receivers
    • Filters and Separators
    • Flare Knockout Drums
    • Scrubbers
    • Reactor Vessels

Review and approve package equipment engineering deliverables including:

    • Chemical Injection Packages
    • Produced Water Treatment Packages
    • Fuel Gas Conditioning Units
    • Air Compressor Packages
    • Nitrogen Generation Packages
    • Desalination Packages
    • Utility Skids
    • Metering Packages

Prepare and review:

    • Equipment Datasheets
    • Material Requisitions (MR)
    • Technical Bid Evaluations (TBE)
    • Technical Queries (TQ)
    • Vendor Document Reviews

Ensure equipment design complies with:

    • ADNOC Offshore Standards
    • ASME Section VIII
    • API Standards
    • TEMA
    • NACE Requirements
    • ISO Standards
    • Project Specifications

Procurement Support

  • Participate in technical clarification meetings with vendors.
  • Evaluate vendor proposals and recommend technically compliant solutions.
  • Review vendor drawings and manufacturing documentation.
  • Support procurement team during bid evaluations and purchase order placement.

Fabrication & Inspection

  • Coordinate with fabrication yards and vendors during manufacturing activities.
  • Review Inspection and Test Plans (ITP).
  • Witness critical FATs and shop inspections when required.
  • Ensure compliance with quality standards and project specifications.

Interface Coordination

Coordinate with:

    • Process Engineering
    • Mechanical Engineering
    • Piping Engineering
    • Structural Engineering
    • Instrumentation & Control
    • Electrical Engineering
    • HSE and Operations Teams

Resolve multidisciplinary design issues and interface concerns.

Construction & Commissioning Support

  • Provide engineering support during construction and offshore installation activities.
  • Review site technical queries and deviation requests.
  • Support pre-commissioning, commissioning, start-up, and performance testing activities.
  • Participate in Mechanical Completion Walkdowns and Punch List closure.

HSE & Quality

Ensure all engineering activities adhere to ADNOC HSE requirements.

Participate in:

    • HAZID
    • HAZOP
    • SIL Reviews
    • Design Reviews
    • Constructability Reviews

Promote safety in design and asset integrity principles throughout project execution.

Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical Engineering from a recognized university.
  • Master's Degree is advantageous.

Experience

  • Minimum 15 years of experience in Oil & Gas projects.
  • Minimum 5 years in a Specialist or Lead Engineer role.
  • Strong experience in ADNOC Offshore, Saudi Aramco, QatarEnergy, or major offshore brownfield/greenfield developments.
  • Experience in PMC and EPC project execution phases.

Technical Expertise

Strong working knowledge of:

  • ASME Section VIII Div.1 & Div.2
  • API 510
  • API 650
  • API 620
  • API 660
  • API 661
  • TEMA Standards
  • NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156
  • Pressure Vessel Design Principles
  • Package Equipment Engineering
  • Offshore Facilities Design
  • Materials Selection and Corrosion Engineering Concepts

Software Knowledge

  • PV Elite
  • Aspen EDR
  • Compress (Desirable)
  • AutoCAD
  • SmartPlant / Aveva Engineering Systems
  • MS Office Applications

description:
Job Title: Technicians & Service Advisors

Employment Type: Full-Time / Part-Time (Non-Exempt)

Pay Range: $11/hr and up

The Opportunity


Whether you are launching your career under the hood or at the front counter, Jiffy Lube is looking for motivated individuals to join our team as either a Technician or a Service Advisor. Our Technicians are essential to delivering fast, high-quality automotive service in a hands-on, team-oriented environment where you’ll learn valuable technical skills to keep vehicles running safely and efficiently. Meanwhile, our Customer Service Advisors serve as the face of the business, acting as the first point of contact to build trust, educate guests on vehicle maintenance, and drive sales. If you enjoy working with your hands, thriving in a high-energy environment, or working directly with people, Jiffy Lube offers a fast-paced workplace that actively invests in your long-term career growth and professional development.


Our service center teams keep people safely on the road — and we’re hiring people who want to build a career doing it. This is a hands-on role where you’ll work in the service bay and with our guests. Some days you’ll spend more time under the hood, some days more time at the counter. Everyone on our team is trained to do both.


No automotive experience required. We provide industry-leading hands-on training, and many of our store managers started in this exact role.


What You’ll Do


• Greet every guest with a friendly, professional approach and create a positive first impression

• Listen to customer concerns and recommend the right maintenance services for their vehicle

• Conduct vehicle inspections and clearly communicate findings to guests and teammates

• Build trust by educating customers on preventative maintenance and what their vehicle actually needs

• Explain services, pricing, and timelines with confidence and transparency

• Perform oil changes, fluid checks, and preventative maintenance services

• Deliver fast, efficient service without cutting corners on quality

• Support teammates across every area of the shop as needed

• Resolve customer concerns quickly and professionally

• Accurately create service orders and process transactions

• Safely guide vehicles into and out of service bays

• Contribute to store sales and service goals

• Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment

• Follow all company safety procedures and operational standards


What We’re Looking For


• Previous automotive, mechanical, customer service, retail, or sales experience is a plus — but not required

• Willingness to learn and jump into hands-on training

• Strong work ethic and a positive attitude

• Comfortable talking with people and explaining things clearly

• Ability to multitask and stay organized in a fast-paced environment

• Comfortable working on your feet for extended periods

• Team-oriented mindset — we cover for each other

• Ability to work flexible schedules, including weekends as needed


Work Environment & Physical Requirements


• Ability to stand for extended periods of time

• Work in a service shop environment with exposure to noise, fumes, and varying temperatures

• Ability to lift up to 50 pounds

• Frequent bending, lifting, and working with tools and equipment

• Ability to occasionally drive customer vehicles


Why Join Our Team?


• Competitive weekly pay

• Bonus and incentive opportunities

• Medical, dental, and vision insurance

• 401(k) with company match

• Paid time off starting Day 1

• Employee discounts

• Industry-leading training programs

• Clear career advancement opportunities

• Team-oriented, supportive work environment


Tell us where you see yourself — under the hood, at the counter, or both. We’ll figure out the right fit together.


Equal Opportunity Employer

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law.

title: Sr. Director, Product Management AI Experiences (VIRTUAL, WA, US, 00000)
description:
Welcome to the intersection of energy and home services. At NRG, we’re driven by our passion to create a smarter, cleaner and more connected future.

Vivint Smart Home, an NRG owned company, is a leading smart home company in the United States, dedicated to redefining the home experience with intelligent products and services. We find purpose in proactively protecting and keeping our customers connected to home, no matter where they are. Join the Smart Home team to create smarter, safer and more sustainable homes.

Position Summary: Sr. Director Product Management AI Experiences

In this vital leadership role, you will serve as the Senior Director of Product Management for AI Experiences, acting as the single-threaded technical product leader responsible for transforming Vivint’s smart home hardware into a proactive, intelligent ecosystem. Operating with a high degree of autonomy, you will serve as the organization's independent strategic engine for software intelligence. You will bridge the gap between complex machine learning architectures and delightful consumer interfaces, defining the experiences that allow the future home to work seamlessly on behalf of our customers—giving back time, keeping them safe, and saving them money.

This role requires a forward-looking product leader with a deep technical understanding of where AI and machine learning are going. You will be responsible for defining a multi-year vision and building "new-to-world" experiences that utilize ambient intelligence, predictive analytics, and computer vision across our entire hardware portfolio. You will lead a team of Technical Product Managers and collaborate with AI data scientists, platform engineers, and hardware architects to turn raw ambient telemetry into deeply personalized, high-value consumer offers.

Primary Responsibilities

Strategic AI Vision & 3-Year Roadmap

  • Next-Gen Experience Strategy: Own the definition, multi-year sequencing, and execution of the AI experience roadmap across the entire Vivint and NRG smart home portfolio.
  • Predictive Futures: Develop a comprehensive 3-year product roadmap rooted in a deep technical understanding of emerging AI/ML capabilities, translating future technological vectors into immediate, high-value customer benefits.
  • New-to-World Innovation: Autonomously identify, scope, and validate "white space" opportunities to deploy net-new, disruptive AI experiences that shift the smart home from a reactive state to an ambient, proactive state.

title: Senior Privacy Analyst Consultant
description:
ABOUT KALLES GROUP:

Everyone deserves to be secure. Our mission at Kalles Group is to help secure the future for companies of all shapes and sizes.

While our expertise spans multiple disciplines, our method remains consistent: building trust and relationship with people -- whether you are a client, a consultant, or--in this case--a candidate.

No matter what role you come from--whether you're an executive or just starting your career-you can expect our highest level of attention and respect. We want to find the right fit for each role, but we also want you to find the right fit for your career.

We believe the best way to show you what our team is like is to treat you like you're already a part of it. We hope you'll consider joining our team of experienced professionals who are building their careers at Kalles Group—and having fun while doing it.

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

Our client, a large global retailer, is building out a new Records of Processing Activities (ROPA) program to support its Canadian operations, largely from the ground up. In this role, you'll partner directly with the client's privacy engineering team and work across a wide range of business units to document how each line of business handles data, translating existing global ROPA structures into accurate, Canada-specific entries.

If you have hands-on ROPA-building experience, are comfortable owning stakeholder relationships independently, and know how to stay organized across a large, multi-threaded workload, we want to speak with you.

You will:

  • Build out a Canadian ROPA program largely from the ground up, partnering directly with the client's privacy engineering team.
  • Lead discovery and requirements-gathering sessions with business stakeholders across approximately 10-12 business units, documenting each unit's systems, processes, and data handling practices.
  • Draft and maintain ROPA entries using established templates, adapting existing global ROPA structures to reflect Canada-specific business processes.
  • Proactively track and follow up on outstanding items across 24+ stakeholders, maintaining clear visibility into what's needed, from whom, and by when.
  • Communicate directly and professionally with senior business stakeholders, including VP-level contacts, without requiring guidance on tone or approach.
  • Participate in daily standups to report progress, plans, and blockers.
  • Keep program leadership copied on business-facing communications for visibility, while operating independently day to day.
  • Recognize appropriate scope boundaries for each ROPA entry, flagging items that extend beyond the intended process rather than pursuing them further.

ABOUT YOU:

Your values:

  • Integrity: You believe in doing the right thing, even when it's uncomfortable, seemingly inefficient, or costly.
  • Purposefulness: You have a desire to serve others with your skillset and an openness to continuous learning and growth.
  • Ownership: You stick to your commitments, follow up with action, and seek clarity in communication & expectations.

Your experience:

  • Proven, hands-on experience building or maintaining ROPAs in a North American context (US, Canada, Mexico, or similar); ROPA structure and methodology are largely consistent across these markets.
  • Prior experience operating at a senior analyst or engineer level within a privacy or GRC program, someone who has owned and driven ROPA-building work directly, not solely contributed as a business subject matter expert.
  • Comfort and professionalism engaging directly with senior stakeholders, including VPs, without requiring coaching on communication style.
  • Strong organizational skills and self-driven follow-up habits, able to track outstanding items at a granular, per-entry level across many concurrent stakeholders.
  • Familiarity with Quebec Law 25 or similar principle-based privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR) a plus, not required for candidates with strong general North American ROPA experience.
  • Comfortable working independently with light day-to-day oversight, while maintaining consistent visibility and communication with leadership.

We'd be especially excited to talk to you if you have:

  • Experience standing up a ROPA or privacy program in a new market or region from scratch.
  • Background working within large, complex, multi-line-of-business organizations.
  • Experience in a consulting or client-facing capacity, comfortable being a trusted outside voice rather than an internal employee.
  • Comfort with a defined-duration engagement and the flexibility to scope your own workload independently.

WHAT WE OFFER:

  • Salary range of $105,000–$135,000, depending on experience and location.
  • Medical, dental, vision, and pharmaceutical coverage.
  • An education stipend of $2,000 annually to put towards your own growth and development.
  • 401(k) and life insurance benefits.
  • 3 weeks of Paid Time Off. PLUS 8 paid company holidays and 2 flexible holidays for anything you want to celebrate!
  • Work/life balance – we know there's more to life than work! We encourage our team to pursue other passions, get outside, and spend time with family. We work with clients and consultants to set expectations for a manageable workload.
  • Opportunities to connect in person and remotely with a passionate, supportive team.

LOCATION:

This role can be performed remotely or in-office in Seattle, WA, depending on candidate location. If you would like to request more information, please reach out to talent@kallesgroup.com.

HOW TO APPLY:

Please fill out the form below (including uploading your most recent resume) and we'll be in touch! We know imposter syndrome can be a barrier to many great applicants. We hope you'll still consider applying. That's why we've made the application process as short and simple as possible.

Even if you're not a fit for the role, you can expect to hear back from us! We want you to have the best experience as a candidate, so please feel free to share feedback at any stage of the process to talent@kallesgroup.com.

Kalles Group is an equal-opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of creed, nationality, race, ethnicity, disability, gender, or other protected class.

University High School is a coeducational independent day school in San Francisco, California, serving approximately 514 students in grades 9-12. Founded in 1975, the school's mission is to challenge each individual to live a life of integrity, inquiry, and purpose larger than the self. UHS is located in the Pacific Heights neighborhood of San Francisco.

Collaboration and Communication

Uphold the UHS Athletics Mission

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
Senior Data Engineer | Python, Vector Databases & AI Data Pipelines | Early Engineer at an AI Platform Rebuilding an Entire Industry's Back Office

  • Salary: £70,000 - £100,000
  • Location: Victoria, central London. 4 days a week on-site, Wednesdays from home

There's a particular kind of frustration that comes from watching an entire industry run on spreadsheets, phone calls and email chains long after the technology to fix it exists. That's the gap this company is closing. They've built an AI assistant that takes over the operational grind for property managers, letting agents and build-to-rent teams: the compliance chasing, the maintenance coordination, the scheduling, the endless admin that eats up most of a property manager's week. Pilot customers are already live across thousands of units, and the feedback has been strong enough that the business is now gearing up for its next funding round.

The team sits at 20-30 people globally, with engineering at around 13 and mostly remote outside the core London group. It's a flat set-up: leads are simply the engineers who've earned it, and everyone reports into the Head of Engineering. Data hasn't had a dedicated owner yet, and you'd be joining right at the point where that's being built, working alongside the team defining the architecture rather than dropping into something already set in stone.

Day to day you'll be building and scaling the systems behind the AI product: real-time pipelines, analytics infrastructure, vector databases and the data workflows that feed the machine learning side of the platform. You'll work closely with the AI and backend engineers to make sure the platform can handle serious volumes of operational data reliably, and you'll have real input into the tooling and technical decisions as the function takes shape.

What They're Looking For (Non-Negotiables)
  • 5+ years in data engineering or backend engineering
  • Strong track record designing and building data pipelines and distributed data systems
  • Relational databases (PostgreSQL preferred, MySQL or similar acceptable)
  • NoSQL databases
  • Vector databases used in modern AI systems
  • Strong Python

What You'll Work With
  • Apache Spark
  • Apache Airflow
  • Kafka
  • Elasticsearch / OpenSearch
  • MongoDB
  • Vector databases such as Qdrant, Milvus or pgvector
  • Pandas and Polars

Nice to Haves
  • JavaScript / Node.js alongside Python
  • Experience on AI or machine learning platforms
  • Stream processing and event-driven architectures
  • Cloud infrastructure (GCP, AWS or Azure)
  • Time in a high-growth startup or early-stage company

Why Join / Projects
You're joining at the point where the data function still has more questions than answers, which means your fingerprints end up on the actual architecture rather than just the code that runs on top of it. You'll get real exposure to the AI and ML side of the business through the vector search and retrieval work, not just traditional pipeline building, and you're close enough to the founders and core engineering team that good ideas don't get lost in layers of process.

If this role peaks your interest, please apply and I’ll give you a call if I think you’re suitable.

Role Description:

IMP's products are trusted by MATs nationwide to manage their finances more efficiently and effectively. Our portfolio spans budgeting, forecasting and reporting in Planner, curriculum financial planning in ICFP, and now Finance and Purchasing, the products that record and control a trust's day-to-day spend. The portfolio is growing, each product serves a loyal and expanding customer base, and each evolves as our customers' needs evolve and as IMP builds its platform ambition.

We are looking for a Product Manager to own IMP Finance and Purchasing, the two products that run a trust's everyday finances. Purchasing helps trusts manage and control their spend. Finance is the transactional system behind it, handling the day-to-day accounting from payment runs to bank reconciliation.

Your job is to deepen and extend these two products as trusts adopt them. That means sharpening what has shipped, validating and delivering the capabilities that will matter most next, and working closely with engineering and design to deliver with rigour and pace. This is a role for someone who combines genuine curiosity about customer problems with the strategic discipline to decide what not to build.

Above all, you will stay close to the user. The trust finance teams and budget holders who work in these products every day are your compass, and a discovery-led understanding of their needs is what shapes what you build.

You will be part of a product team that is actively shifting from reactive delivery to discovery-led development, and you will play a leading role in embedding that change within your squad and modelling it for the wider team.

Key responsibilities:

1. Product Strategy and Vision

  • Define and evolve the vision for the Finance and Purchasing products in response to customer insight, market signals, and business goals.

  • Own your product roadmap, balancing improvements that deepen the value of what has shipped with new capabilities that extend the products' position in MAT finance and purchasing.

  • Collaborate with the Head of Product and leadership to align your products' direction with IMP's broader platform strategy and commercial objectives.

  • Maintain a clear view of the competitive landscape across finance and purchasing software, and how your products can continue to differentiate within the MAT sector.

2. Customer Discovery and Insight

  • Own discovery for your products, from identifying problem areas and validating hypotheses through to defining success metrics before any build commitment.

  • Conduct regular customer interviews, observation sessions, and contextual research with MAT finance teams, business managers and budget holders.

  • Synthesise insight from multiple sources, including customer interviews, support data, usage analytics and NPS, into clear problem statements and opportunity assessments.

  • Build and test prototypes and lightweight MVPs before committing to build, working iteratively with design to refine solutions based on real user feedback.

  • Champion the voice of the customer across the business, ensuring product decisions are grounded in evidence rather than assumption.

3. Roadmap Ownership and Prioritisation

  • Own and communicate your product roadmap, making prioritisation decisions that balance customer impact, business value, and technical feasibility.

  • Define and monitor key product metrics that validate whether your products are delivering the outcomes customers and the business need, distinguishing leading from lagging indicators.

  • Work with engineering and design to translate roadmap priorities into well-scoped delivery cycles with clear acceptance criteria and measurable outcomes.

  • Collaborate with other PMs and POs across the IMP product team on cross-product dependencies and shared planning, including where Finance and Purchasing connect to Planner and the wider platform.

4. Delivery Partnership

  • Work closely with your engineering squad and designers throughout the delivery cycle, from refining the problem through to reviewing shipped features against defined outcomes.

  • Ensure your squad has clear context on what they are building and why, not just how.

  • Use AI tooling to improve the quality and speed of specifications, synthesis, and product analysis.

  • Monitor product performance post-launch and drive iterative improvements based on data and customer feedback.

5. Cross-Functional Collaboration and Go-to-Market

  • Work with Support, Implementation, and Sales to consolidate customer feedback and ensure product developments are well communicated and adopted.

  • Partner with Customer Success and Marketing to shape go-to-market activities for significant Finance and Purchasing releases.

  • Represent your products' customer perspective in cross-functional conversations, ensuring alignment across the business on priorities and trade-offs.

Skills, experience, and attributes :

  • A track record of product management or product ownership in B2B SaaS, typically 4+ years, though we care more about demonstrated capability than an exact year count.

  • Demonstrable experience owning an established product, evolving it meaningfully in response to customer need and commercial opportunity.

  • Strong customer discovery capability. You have conducted interviews, synthesised insights, and shaped product direction from evidence rather than assumption.

  • Experience defining and tracking product metrics to validate impact, including leading indicators that predict retention and adoption.

  • Strong prioritisation judgement. You can make and defend difficult trade-off decisions with clarity.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management, including the ability to push back with data and offer alternatives rather than just saying no.

  • Comfortable working autonomously in a remote environment and driving forward without close supervision.

  • Experience with product management tools ( Monday.com , Jira, Azure DevOps, or similar).

  • Active user of AI tooling for product management work and curious about how to apply it further.

  • Familiarity with Agile/Scrum methodologies.

Desirable:

  • Experience in product management of finance, accounting, purchasing, procurement, or spend-management software.

  • A strong working understanding of core finance and accounting processes, such as budgeting, nominal and cost centre coding, the requisition-to-invoice cycle, and approval and control workflows, whether gained from building software in this space or from hands-on finance experience.

  • Knowledge of MAT budgeting, curriculum financial planning, or school funding workflows.

  • Understanding of MAT structures, the UK education landscape, or school finance governance.

  • Experience in EdTech, school MIS, or education finance systems.

  • Experience working in or alongside sectors where the buyer and the daily user are different people, and where financial controls, approvals and audit trails matter.

  • Formal product discovery training (Continuous Discovery Habits, Prod MBA, Product School, or equivalent).

  • Experience using Claude for specifications, analysis, and customer insight synthesis, or Lovable for rapid prototyping.

  • Life assurance (4 x basic salary)

  • Encouraged and funded CPD

title: Robotics Autonomy Engineer - Triage
description:
FieldAI’s Irvine team is where embodied AI meets real robots, real sensors, and real field deployments. Based in the heart of Southern California’s robotics ecosystem, we build risk-aware, reliable, field-ready AI systems that solve the hardest problems in robotics and unlock the full potential of embodied intelligence. If you want your work to ship, get tested on hardware, and improve through real deployments, Irvine is the place. We go beyond typical data-driven approaches or pure transformer-only architectures, combining rigorous engineering with learning systems proven in globally deployed solutions that deliver results today and get better every time our robots run in the field.

About the Job

Field AI is building the future of autonomy—from rugged terrain to real-world deployment. We’re on a mission to develop intelligent, adaptable robotic systems that operate beyond simulation and thrive in unpredictable environments. As our Robotics Autonomy Engineer – Triage, you’ll be the fastest link between what our robots experience in the field and how our autonomy stack improves, reproducing behaviors, finding root causes, and driving rapid fixes and tests that make every deployment smoother than the last. You’ll be part of a deeply technical team advancing real-world robotic capabilities through cutting-edge research, simulation tools, and field validation. If solving hard puzzles on real robots and seeing your fixes land in the field within days excites you, and you want to work where your code hits the ground (literally)—this is your role. This is Field AI

What You’ll Get To Do

  • Triage incoming reports from field deployments and customer sites, assess impact, and decide what gets fixed now, what gets routed, and what gets tracked.
  • Reproduce field behaviors from logs, telemetry, and recordings, both in simulation and on hardware.
  • Root cause behaviors that span perception, localization, planning, control, and integration boundaries, and ship targeted fixes quickly.
  • Turn every fix into a regression test, scenario, or hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) check so the improvement holds.
  • Build triage tooling for log analysis, event detection, and trend tracking across robots and sites.
  • Run structured test campaigns before releases and help decide when a build is ready for the field.
  • Share clear findings and summaries with owning teams, and champion design improvements when patterns emerge.
  • Travel occasionally to deployment sites to see robots operate firsthand and support field teams

What You Have

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
  • 2+ years of experience working on real autonomous systems in industry or research.
  • Strong debugging skills across the full autonomy stack, from sensors and drivers to planning and control.
  • Solid programming skills in C++ and Python in Linux-based environments.
  • Familiarity with robotics middleware such as ROS/ROS 2.
  • Experience analyzing logs, telemetry, and recorded robot data to understand system behavior.
  • Comfort working quickly with incomplete information, and communicating clearly with engineers and field teams.

The Extras That Set You Apart

  • Experience with release testing, validation, or quality engineering for autonomous systems.
  • Experience building simulation based regression pipelines or hardware-in-the-loop test setups.
  • Experience with data pipelines and event detection over large volumes of robot data.
  • Experience with incident management or defect tracking in a fast moving engineering team.
  • Time spent in the field with deployed robots or autonomous vehicles.
  • Familiarity with continuous integration and automated test infrastructure.
  • Experience with legged, wheeled, or humanoid platforms.
Our salary range is generous and we consider each individual’s background and experience when determining final compensation. Base pay may vary based on role scope, job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and the Irvine, California market.
Why Join FieldAI in Irvine?
In Irvine, you will work where the robots are. Our local team builds and tests systems on real hardware with real sensors, then ships them to operate in unstructured, previously unknown environments around the world. We are solving one of robotics’ hardest challenges: reliable deployment outside the lab. Our Field Foundational Models™ raise the bar for perception, planning, localization, and manipulation, with an emphasis on explainability and safety for real-world use.
You will collaborate with a world-class team that thrives on creativity, resilience, and bold thinking. We bring deep experience from organizations such as DeepMind, NASA JPL, Boston Dynamics, NVIDIA, Amazon, Tesla Autopilot, Cruise, Zoox, Toyota Research Institute, and SpaceX, along with a track record of field deployments and strong performance in DARPA challenge segments.
Be Part of the Next Robotics Revolution
We are looking for builders who want their work to leave the whiteboard and show up on robots. If you enjoy tackling tough, uncharted questions and working across disciplines, you will find your people here. Our teams span AI, software, robotics engineering, product, field deployment, and technical communication, all focused on shipping systems that perform in the real world.
Our headquarters is in Irvine, and we partner closely with teams there as well as colleagues across the US and around the world. Join us in Southern California and help define what dependable, field-ready autonomy looks like.
We value diverse perspectives and are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace. We evaluate candidates and employees based on merit, qualifications, and performance, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, or any other legally protected status.

title: Robotics Autonomy Engineer - Safety
description:
FieldAI’s Irvine team is where embodied AI meets real robots, real sensors, and real field deployments. Based in the heart of Southern California’s robotics ecosystem, we build risk-aware, reliable, field-ready AI systems that solve the hardest problems in robotics and unlock the full potential of embodied intelligence. If you want your work to ship, get tested on hardware, and improve through real deployments, Irvine is the place. We go beyond typical data-driven approaches or pure transformer-only architectures, combining rigorous engineering with learning systems proven in globally deployed solutions that deliver results today and get better every time our robots run in the field.

About the Job

Field AI is building the future of autonomy—from rugged terrain to real-world deployment. We’re on a mission to develop intelligent, adaptable robotic systems that operate beyond simulation and thrive in unpredictable environments. As our Robotics Autonomy Engineer – Safety, you’ll own and advance the independent safety layer that keeps our robots safe around people, equipment, and terrain no matter what the rest of the autonomy stack decides. You’ll be part of a deeply technical team advancing real-world robotic capabilities through cutting-edge research, simulation tools, and field validation. If building the guarantees that let robots earn trust in the real world excites you, and you want to work where your code hits the ground (literally)—this is your role. This is Field AI.

What You’ll Get To Do

  • Own and evolve the safety layer that runs independently of perception, planning, and learned policies, and extend it to new wheeled, legged, and humanoid platforms
  • Build runtime monitors and collision avoidance backstops that check every commanded motion against the environment before it reaches the robot
  • Enforce speed, zone, terrain, and proximity limits, and define the safe operating envelope for each platform and deployment
  • Design fallback and minimal risk behaviors, from graceful slow down to safe stop, and the logic that decides when to trigger them
  • Build watchdogs and health monitoring across sensors, compute, communication, and actuation, so the robot always knows when it can trust itself
  • Lead hazard analysis and safety case development for new platforms and new deployments
  • Verify the safety layer in simulation, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing, and field trials, with coverage that grows with every deployment
  • Work with planning, control, locomotion, and integration teams so the nominal stack plans and moves within the safety envelope

What You Have

  • Master’s degree or higher in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or a Bachelor’s degree with substantial hands-on experience on safety related autonomous systems
  • 2+ years of experience developing safety, monitoring, or fallback systems for robots or autonomous vehicles
  • Strong grounding in classical planning and control, such as collision checking and trajectory validation
  • Experience writing deterministic, real time, resource bounded C++ for systems where correctness matters more than features
  • Solid Python skills for tooling, analysis, and test automation in Linux-based environments
  • A verification mindset: you think in terms of assumptions, failure modes, coverage, and evidence
  • Familiarity with safety standards for mobile robots and autonomous systems (e.g., ISO 13482, ISO 3691-4, ISO 26262)
  • Familiarity with robotics middleware such as ROS/ROS 2, and with robot sensors such as LiDAR, depth cameras, and IMUs

The Extras That Set You Apart

  • Functional safety experience in autonomous vehicles, industrial robots, or aerospace
  • Experience with runtime assurance architectures that wrap a learned or complex controller
  • Experience with formal or set based safety methods applied to real robots
  • Experience defining operational design domains and monitoring when a system is outside them
  • Experience with redundant sensing, safety rated hardware, or safety rated communication
  • Experience taking a robotic product through safety assessment or certification
  • Experience with legged or humanoid platforms, where balance and contact make safety envelopes harder to define
Our salary range is generous and we consider each individual’s background and experience when determining final compensation. Base pay may vary based on role scope, job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and the Irvine, California market.
Why Join FieldAI in Irvine?
In Irvine, you will work where the robots are. Our local team builds and tests systems on real hardware with real sensors, then ships them to operate in unstructured, previously unknown environments around the world. We are solving one of robotics’ hardest challenges: reliable deployment outside the lab. Our Field Foundational Models™ raise the bar for perception, planning, localization, and manipulation, with an emphasis on explainability and safety for real-world use.
You will collaborate with a world-class team that thrives on creativity, resilience, and bold thinking. We bring deep experience from organizations such as DeepMind, NASA JPL, Boston Dynamics, NVIDIA, Amazon, Tesla Autopilot, Cruise, Zoox, Toyota Research Institute, and SpaceX, along with a track record of field deployments and strong performance in DARPA challenge segments.
Be Part of the Next Robotics Revolution
We are looking for builders who want their work to leave the whiteboard and show up on robots. If you enjoy tackling tough, uncharted questions and working across disciplines, you will find your people here. Our teams span AI, software, robotics engineering, product, field deployment, and technical communication, all focused on shipping systems that perform in the real world.
Our headquarters is in Irvine, and we partner closely with teams there as well as colleagues across the US and around the world. Join us in Southern California and help define what dependable, field-ready autonomy looks like.

title: Senior Security Engineer, Zero Trust Access (Zscaler ZPA)
description:
Job Description

Senior Security Engineer, Zero Trust Access (Zscaler ZPA)



Sydney or Melbourne - Hybrid (1-3 days per week)



If your Zscaler experience is URL filtering, SSL inspection and cloud app control, this is not your role.



We are looking for the other kind of Zscaler person. The one who has stood up App Connectors, built application segments, written access policy from a blank page, and lived through the part of a VPN decommissioning where the last forty legacy applications refuse to move.



The organisation


A large Australian enterprise with a complex hybrid estate, thousands of staff and contractors, and an internal application landscape that has accumulated over decades. Zscaler is already in place. What is missing is a single owner for the private access side of it.



What you will own


You are the person accountable for Zscaler Private Access end to end. Not a ticket queue, and not one work stream inside someone else's programme.




  • Application discovery across the estate, including the systems nobody documented and the ones a business unit stood up quietly six years ago

  • The access policy model itself: who reaches what, from which devices, in what posture, and how employees, contractors and third parties are treated differently

  • App Connector architecture, placement and resilience across on-premises and cloud environments

  • Segment groups, server groups, client forwarding policy and posture profiles, designed as a coherent standard rather than assembled case by case

  • The onboarding standard that application owners follow, and the exception and change process that sits around it

  • Ongoing access review, reporting and the evidence trail that stands up to audit

  • Driving the retirement of legacy remote access, and holding the line when someone senior asks for a bypass



What we are looking for



  • Demonstrable hands-on ownership of Zscaler Private Access at enterprise scale, not exposure to it inside a wider platform role

  • Evidence you designed the policy rather than executed someone else's design

  • A network security lineage. Firewalls, routing, traffic inspection and segmentation thinking, rather than a purely Microsoft security background

  • Experience taking applications off a VPN and the political reality that comes with it

  • The ability to write it down properly. Design documentation, configuration standards, runbooks and operational handover material that other engineers can actually work from

  • Confidence holding a technical position in front of application owners and senior stakeholders who want an exception

  • Zscaler certification (ZCCA-PA or above) is a strong signal, though delivery evidence matters more than the certificate



Adjacent micro-segmentation experience will be viewed favourably. The disciplines are close relatives.



What this role is not


Worth being direct, because it saves everyone time.



  • Not a secure web gateway or proxy administration role

  • Not a governance, risk and compliance role. This is technical policy ownership, not framework and audit work

  • Not a broad platform engineering role covering endpoint, email and mobile device management. The scope here is deliberately narrow and deep



Why it is worth a conversation


Single-platform ownership roles at this scale are rare. Most organisations either spread the work across four engineers who each own a slice, or hand it to an integrator who builds it and leaves.



This one is yours to own, with the mandate and the seniority to make decisions rather than recommend them.



Applying


Apply through this advert, or contact Will at RONIN directly for a confidential conversation. Happy to talk through the detail before you decide whether it is worth your time.

title: Product Data Scientist
description:
Title : Product Data Scientist

Location : Remote Mexico

Industry Experience: Banking / Financial Services – Required

Domain: Consumer Lending / FinTech preferred



Abo About You

5+ years of experience in a hybrid analytics/data science role (e.g., analytics consulting, product data science, applied statistics) with a track record of directly informing product decisions; bachelor’s degree or higher in a quantitative field, or equivalent combination of education and experience

You have strong grounding in statistics and experimentation — hypothesis testing, causal inference, experiment design, and you can explain the difference between a significant result and a meaningful one

You’re fluent in SQL and at least one scripting/statistical language (Python or R), and you’re comfortable enough with data engineering fundamentals (pipelines, transformations, data modeling) to build what you need and partner effectively with engineers on the rest

You can develop, validate, and communicate the tradeoffs of statistical and machine learning models, and you know when a simpler model or a well-designed experiment beats a complex one

You use AI tools in your day-to-day work — for exploratory analysis, documentation, and accelerating routine analytics — and you know when their outputs need scrutiny before they touch a product decision

You think like a consultant: you get to the real question behind the question, structure ambiguous problems, and land on recommendations stakeholders can act on

You have good judgment about rigor versus speed, and you don’t cut corners on measurement integrity just to hit a deadline

You’re a clear communicator who can flex between a technical conversation with engineering and a decision-focused conversation with product and business stakeholders

You’re curious about how data, experimentation, and AI can change what’s possible in consumer lending products, and you’re always looking for a better way to answer the question

Background in fintech, consumer lending, or home improvement/contractor financing

Experience with CDP platforms, event instrumentation tooling (e.g., Segment, mParticle, Amplitude), or experimentation platforms

Prior experience embedded directly with product teams in an agile/scrum environment

📋 Job Information

  • Job Title: Bilingual Logistics Coordinator (Oversized & Car Carrier Freight)
  • Job ID: FRAPAM2H
  • Industry: Freight Brokerage and Logistics
  • Location: LATAM
  • Job Status: Full Time
  • Work Schedule: Thursday - Monday, 8 am to 5 pm (EST) (Tuesday & Wednesday off)
  • Compensation: $1500 per month
  • Target Start Date: ASAP

🧩 Role Overview

About the Client:

Our client is an established, family-owned logistics service provider and freight brokerage dedicated to empowering commerce through efficient and innovative supply chain solutions. Built on a foundation of integrity, sustainability, and long-term relationships, they operate as a deeply trusted partner for businesses across multiple sectors.
They pride themselves on a culture of constant communication and total transparency, providing 24/7 round-the-clock service to ensure time-sensitive freight is delivered seamlessly. By blending industry experience with personalized care, they provide an agile, fast-paced environment where employees are empowered to grow and directly contribute to the success of global trade.

About the Role:

We are seeking a highly motivated and solutions-oriented Bilingual Logistics Coordinator to join our team. In this role, you will start with a strong focus on tracking, tracing, and operational execution, with a clear trajectory to advance into a commission-earning Account Manager role.

The ideal candidate possesses exceptional customer service, problem-solving abilities, and a basic foundation in logistics operations. Rather than general freight, this role prioritizes experience in specialized freight sectors, specifically Produce and Open Deck (Oversize, Overweight, and Overwidth) cargo.


🔑 Key Responsibilities:

  • Provide high-level track and trace coverage, ensuring real-time shipment visibility and accurate system updates.
  • Proactively problem-solve operational hurdles during weekend and peak-season shifts to prevent delivery delays.
  • Maintain accurate communication with carriers regarding load specifics, pickup/delivery addresses, and schedule adherence.
  • Learn and adapt to market pricing platforms to effectively quote and negotiate competitive rates with open-deck and produce carriers.
  • Smoothly transition from an internal operations support position to a client-facing account management role based on performance.

🎯 Qualifications & Skills:

  • Bilingual: Fluent in both Spanish and English (Required).
  • Core Experience: 1–2 years of experience in track and trace, logistics coordination, or a freight brokerage setting.
  • Niche Expertise: Proven experience or strong familiarity handling Produce and/or Open Deck (Oversize / Overweight / Overwidth) freight is highly preferred.
  • Competencies: Strong negotiation skills, confident telephone demeanor, and excellent multi-tasking capabilities.
  • Problem-Solving: Strong customer service mentality with the capacity to stay calm and resourceful under high-pressure, peak-season conditions.
  • Systems & Software:
    • Experience with Load Boards (DAT, Truckstop) is strongly preferred.
    • Experience with Transportation Management Systems (specifically Tai Software) is strongly preferred.
    • Experience with 3CX dialer systems is a plus.

Tiered Career Path:

  • Tier C (Entry / Track & Trace): Focuses heavily on track and trace, answering driver calls, verifying pickup details, and providing proactive client updates.
  • Tier B (Operations Specialist): Introduces market-rate quoting, carrier sourcing, and carrier rate negotiations.
  • Tier A / S (Account Manager): Full management of key clients, independent quoting, and carrier book management. At this stage, the role transitions to a Monday–Friday schedule.
